query_snapshot: What two temperature-related material-selection concerns does NASA SP-8119 identify for cryogenic disconnects?
final_answer:
Evidence-grounded answer:

- NASA SP-8119 states that some seal materials (for example, Teflon/plastic seals) are very brittle at cryogenic/low temperatures and can fracture, causing seal failure and related problems. [nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 65-66, chunk af0b8a8f; nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 101-102, chunk 95e11df8; nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 132-133, chunk fb39e662]
- NASA SP-8119 warns that materials with widely different coefficients of thermal expansion (differential thermal contraction/shrinkage) can produce large bolting problems, improper clearances or fits, unloaded seals, and misalignment; the report recommends using materials with similar coefficients of expansion or locating the material with greatest shrinkage appropriately. [nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 85-88, chunk 91eb9fc5; nbscircular592.pdf, pp. 63-64, chunk 80d16705]
